newsitem.title: USA: Conn. Gov. Rowland insists on tax cuts - report.
newsitem.headline: Conn. Gov. Rowland insists on tax cuts - report.

text.p: Republican Gov. John Rowland is determined to cut Connecticut's income tax even if it means a bitter fight with Democrats who control both chambers of the legislature, the Hartford Courant reported Wednesday.
Rowland told the Courant in an interview that he is preparing for "a showdown," and that he is willing to keep legislators at the state Capitol all summer unless they meet his demands.
The current legislative session is scheduled to end June 4.
Rowland said he will veto any budget bill that does not include major tax cuts.
Connecticut Democrats have different priorities, and many favor cutting the property tax.

Rowland said he is willing to compromise with Democrats to some extent, and will not demand that the legislature approve his enteire package of $365 million in income tax cuts and $65 million in gasoline tax cuts.
But he did not give a specific figure that would satisfy him.
Rowland, who is up for re-election in 1998, has vowed to eliminate the state income tax over five years. The level of tax cuts is expected to be a major issue in his campaign.
